Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0155", "row_sha256": "d9dda12474cae91de29f265155be60a7560cdb8d3df0f0df6b217d253847e0ee", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "we need a self contained internal update for the team about our move from HarborShare to AtlasDocs, not a general guide to moving files and not a launch announcement. write it as an ordinary update for the 14 people who use the workspace, and keep it grounded in the details below. the inventory snapshot was taken february 27. it found 612 active documents in the three folders included in this move: 248 project briefs, 191 field logs and 173 templates. there are also 77 archived items, but those are out of scope and should stay on HarborShare. personal drafts are out of scope too and should not be counted in the migration. say clearly what is and is not included, because a few people have already asked if the old archive folders are coming along.

the team began the move on march 4 with a pilot batch of 36 documents. that batch was used to check folder paths and the basic access setup, not to test every possible kind of file. we found that two folder names on AtlasDocs did not match the labels people knew from HarborShare, so those labels were corrected before the next batch. please mention that change without making it sound like the underlying documents were renamed. there was also a permissions check with the project leads. each of the 14 team members should be able to read the shared project briefs and field logs; editing access is limited to the 6 document owners. the owners are Maya Chen, Idris Bell, Nora Patel, Theo Grant, Sam Okafor and Elise Ward. the rest of the team should not be described as having editing access.

we moved the files in batches after the pilot. by the march 15 checkpoint, 508 of the 612 in-scope documents had been copied to AtlasDocs. 476 of those copied items had been checked against their HarborShare versions, while 32 copied items were still waiting for review. the other 104 in-scope documents had not yet been copied. don't combine those numbers in a way that makes it sound like all 612 have moved, and keep the checked, awaiting review and not-yet-copied groups distinct. the review list includes 9 documents whose file names need comparison with the source and 11 documents where the owner or access setting still needs a second check. those are counts within the 32 awaiting review, not extra files on top of the 32. the remaining 12 in that group have no issue noted yet; they're just still in the review queue. don't say any of those checks have passed.

we've had a few practical snags, and the update should explain them in a neutral way. two people reported that a preview opened an older copy rather than the new one. the source files were still present on HarborShare when they saw that, and the team has not established whether both reports had the same cause. one field log also displayed its date in a different format after copying; its content was not reported as missing. we need to say that this display difference is being checked, not call it fixed. on march 12, Idris wrote, “I can find the folder, but the preview still opens the old copy.” include the quote as an ordinary reported comment, with his name and date. don't claim it represents everyone's experience.

please describe the schedule carefully. the team started on march 4, the current count is from the march 15 checkpoint, and the remaining copy work is planned to continue through march 22. that's a plan, not confirmation that the work will finish on that day. if the reviews or copy checks find a problem, the affected item will stay on HarborShare until it has been checked; don't imply that a deadline overrides that condition. the old workspace is due to become read-only on march 30, but that change has not happened yet. three vendor-linked templates need their HarborShare versions available in read-only form through april 2. don't say those three can be removed on march 30, and don't suggest that the entire old workspace stays writable until april 2. explain the distinction between the general read-only date and that limited access exception.

include a short numbered section that makes the next steps easy to scan. it should cover continuing the copying through march 22, completing the 32 pending reviews, and confirming the owner and access settings before the old workspace changes to read-only. make clear that these are upcoming steps, not completed work. it is okay to mention the 9 filename comparisons and 11 owner/access checks in the review step, but keep them inside the 32-item total. don't add a new owner, a new date, a new system or a promise that a check will succeed.

end with a distinct final section titled “Current assessment.” preserve the status and its limits there rather than writing a generic summary: as of march 15, 508 of 612 in-scope documents were copied, 476 were checked, 32 copied items remained under review, and 104 had not been copied. the 77 archived items and personal drafts remain outside the migration scope. the march 22 completion date is planned, not confirmed; any item with an unresolved copy or review issue stays on HarborShare until checked. HarborShare is due to become read-only march 30, while the three vendor-linked templates require read-only access through april 2. don't turn that assessment into approval to close HarborShare or claim the migration is complete. use connected paragraphs for the update, include the quote and numbered section naturally, and leave the assessment as the final section with no extra wrap-up after it.", "output": "Write a self-contained internal team update about the move from HarborShare to AtlasDocs. Address the 14 people who use the workspace. Keep the update focused on this migration rather than giving general file-migration guidance or presenting a launch announcement. Use the facts below and do not imply that any work or checks have been completed unless stated.

### Scope and setup

The February 27 inventory identified 612 active documents in the three folders included in the move: 248 project briefs, 191 field logs, and 173 templates. The 77 archived items are out of scope and will remain on HarborShare. Personal drafts are also out of scope and should not be counted as part of the migration. Make this distinction clear, including in light of questions about whether the old archive folders are moving.

The team began with a 36-document pilot batch on March 4. The pilot checked folder paths and basic access setup; it did not test every possible file type. Two AtlasDocs folder labels differed from the familiar HarborShare labels. Those labels were corrected before the next batch; the underlying documents were not renamed.

The permissions check with project leads established the intended access: all 14 team members should be able to read the shared project briefs and field logs, while editing access is limited to the six document owners: Maya Chen, Idris Bell, Nora Patel, Theo Grant, Sam Okafor, and Elise Ward. Do not describe the other team members as having editing access.

### Migration status and issues

By the March 15 checkpoint, 508 of the 612 in-scope documents had been copied to AtlasDocs. Of those 508, 476 had been checked against their HarborShare versions and 32 were still awaiting review. The remaining 104 in-scope documents had not yet been copied. Keep these three groups distinct; do not suggest that all 612 documents have moved.

The 32-item review group includes 9 documents whose file names still need comparison with the source and 11 for which the owner or access setting needs a second check. These counts are included within the 32, not additional items. The other 12 have no issue noted yet but remain in the review queue. Do not say that any of the outstanding checks have passed.

Describe the reported snags neutrally. Two people said a preview opened an older copy rather than the new one. The source files were still present on HarborShare when they saw this, and the team has not established whether the reports had the same cause. One field log displayed its date in a different format after copying; no missing content was reported. Say that the display difference is being checked, not that it has been fixed. Include this ordinary reported comment with its attribution: on March 12, Idris wrote, “I can find the folder, but the preview still opens the old copy.” Do not imply that his comment represents everyone’s experience.

### Timing and next steps

The move began on March 4. The current counts are from the March 15 checkpoint, and the remaining copy work is planned to continue through March 22. This is a plan, not confirmation that the work will finish on that date. If a copy or review check finds a problem, the affected item will stay on HarborShare until it has been checked; do not imply that the planned date overrides this condition.

HarborShare is due to become read-only on March 30, but it has not changed to read-only yet. Three vendor-linked templates need their HarborShare versions available in read-only form through April 2. Distinguish this limited access exception from the general March 30 read-only date: do not say the three templates can be removed on March 30, or that the entire old workspace will stay writable until April 2.

Include a short numbered section identifying these upcoming steps, without presenting them as completed:
1. Continue copying the remaining documents through March 22.
2. Complete the review of the 32 pending items, including the 9 filename comparisons and 11 owner or access checks within that total.
3. Confirm owner and access settings before HarborShare changes to read-only.

### Current assessment

End with a distinct section titled “Current assessment.” State that, as of March 15, 508 of 612 in-scope documents had been copied, 476 had been checked, 32 copied items remained under review, and 104 had not been copied. The 77 archived items and personal drafts remain outside the migration scope. The March 22 completion date is planned, not confirmed, and any item with an unresolved copy or review issue stays on HarborShare until checked. HarborShare is due to become read-only on March 30, while the three vendor-linked templates require read-only access through April 2. Do not frame this assessment as approval to close HarborShare or claim the migration is complete. Use connected paragraphs throughout the update, include the quote and numbered section naturally, and put no additional wrap-up after “Current assessment.”"}]
